name: apply_patch
description:
Change files with a patch, in either of two formats.

The envelope:

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: path/new.py
+every line of the new file, each prefixed with +
*** Update File: path/app.py
*** Move to: path/main.py        (optional rename)
@@ def greet():                  (optional: a line to find first)
 unchanged line
-removed line
+added line
*** Delete File: path/old.txt
*** End Patch

Or a unified diff (as `git diff` writes it): `--- a/<file>` and `+++ b/<file>` lines, then hunks starting `@@ -old,count +new,count @@`. Without those two lines, name the file with `path`. The line numbers are only a hint; the context lines must match the file exactly.

- Every changed hunk needs a few unchanged context lines (prefixed with a space) so it can be found.
- New files: every line starts with + (a unified diff starts with --- /dev/null).
- All files in one patch are applied, or none are.

patch.description: The whole patch: from *** Begin Patch to *** End Patch, or a unified diff

path.description: A unified diff without ---/+++ lines: the file it changes
